message.content:
(1) Overall layout structure: MATCH – Both use a left navigation sidebar and a main content area with top-aligned headers and bottom-aligned action bars.
(2) Information architecture: DIFF – Image 2 places "Search for lost data" buttons inside the drive cards and adds "Healthy" status text, whereas Image 1 uses a single global CTA at the bottom right.
(3) Color palette family: MATCH – Both utilize a light theme with white backgrounds, light blue sidebars, and primary blue accents for interactive elements.
(4) Typography scale: MATCH – Both follow a similar hierarchy with large bold headers, medium-weight sub-headers, and smaller meta-text for drive statistics.
(5) Control geometry: DIFF – Image 2 uses taller, more detailed cards for drives containing internal CTAs, while Image 1 uses compact icon-based cards; Image 2 also uses full-width buttons for specific locations.
(6) Primary CTA placement: DIFF – Image 1 features one prominent "Search" button in the bottom-right corner of the footer, while Image 2 distributes the action into individual card buttons and a secondary footer button.

VERDICT: STRUCTURALLY_DIVERGENT – While the high-level zones are similar, the re-implementation significantly alters the interaction model by moving the primary action from a global footer button into individual component-level controls.
